title: core.reputation.signal_recorded v1
description: Published by CORE when a reputation signal is recorded for a subject, exactly once per producer reference. Carries the reported fact and nothing derived: no running average, count or score. A total computed at publication time would be computed without any signal recorded concurrently with it, so two events about one subject could each carry a different total with no way to order them; a consumer that needs a standing accumulates this stream, which it receives exactly-once, or asks CORE for the derived standing.

reputation_signal_id.description: CORE's identifier for the recorded signal.

organization_id.description: The tenant the signal belongs to. Stated on every reputation event, so a consumer never has to query CORE to scope one.

subject_type.description: The kind of CORE entity the signal is about.

subject_id.description: The identity or organization the signal is about.

signal_kind.description: The declared kind of signal. A closed vocabulary: an unknown kind counts towards nothing and is refused rather than stored.

rating_value.description: The reported rating, present only for a service_rating and null for every other kind.

source_system.description: The producer that reported the signal.

source_reference.description: The producer's own reference for the report. Unique per tenant and producer; this is what makes ingestion exactly-once.

occurred_at.description: When the producer says the fact happened.

recorded_at.description: When CORE recorded it, on CORE's clock. Ordering uses this, so one producer's skew cannot reorder another's facts.
